spec: dispatch://LEGION-33/spec version 2 is binding (Acceptance 1-8, Design, Errors, Rejected). This plan orders the work and fixes the choices the spec left to the planner; it re-decides nothing the spec settles.
workflowRecommendation: One implementer, one PR on legion/LEGION-33. Steps 1 (Go listener) and 2 (state schema) are independent; step 3 (reducers) needs step 2; step 4 (docs) is independent. Work test-first per step: write the named failing test, make it pass, move on. Run the whole verification list (step 5) once at the end, not per step.
concerns: Deploy skew is by design: until the host listener is redeployed AND the daemon restarted on this code, behaviour is exactly today's (every push counts) plus one warn line per unclassifiable push on a red PR. The daemon change is safe against an old listener (Acceptance 3). The redeploy is the architect's post-merge action item for Sami, not part of this PR.

Wire nuance (not a spec defect, but the implementer must know it): normalize.go's payloadJSON drops empty-string fields, so a push whose commits array is empty carries NO changed_paths key on the wire while changed_paths_truncated is still "false". The daemon therefore keys 'listener predates this change' on changed_paths_truncated being ABSENT, never on changed_paths being absent. Acceptance 6's 'empty changed_paths' is asserted in Go as the key being omitted from the decoded payload (the existing `omitted` list in TestGithubPayloadFields).

The live PR #966 (LEGION-23) sits at fixAttempts=6 with a red-by-design check. Because the migration leaves blockedAttempts absent (honest: nothing was recorded), its next red settlement after the upgraded daemon starts publishes pr-blocked exactly once more, then never again until fixAttempts grows. Bounded, and the LEGION-23 architect already knows about the noise.

Accepted rare interleaving under the spec's literal take-back rule: fixAttempts N-1 already published (blockedAttempts=N-1), a synchronize counts to N, CI settles red and publishes for N, THEN the late handoff-only push webhook takes the count back to N-1 and forgets N. A later failing-set change at that head republishes pr-blocked for N-1. Needs a push webhook delayed past a CI settlement (minutes); spec-conformant ('forgotten so the next real fix publishes it again'); do not 'fix' it in this PR.

stateFields.where: packages/daemon/src/daemon/legion-state.ts — `PrState` interface (line ~78) and `PrStateSchema` (line ~261, strict). All three are OPTIONAL; absent is the starting value for every record, which is why the migration is a pure version bump.

headCounted.semantics: Present exactly when the current headSha's arrival in resetPrHead incremented fixAttempts (prior verdict was red and no pending push classified this sha handoff-only). A later handoff-only push webhook whose `after` equals headSha takes the attempt back and deletes it; the next resetPrHead sets or deletes it afresh. Never written as `false` — literal true keeps one representation of 'not counted' (absent), mirroring reviewDecision's set/delete handling.

pendingPush.type: pendingPush?: { sha: string; handoffOnly: boolean }  (zod: z.object({ sha: z.string().min(1), handoffOnly: z.boolean() }).strict().optional())
pendingPush.semantics: The latest push webhook's classification for a head that has not arrived yet (push `after` !== headSha). A later push for another not-yet-arrived sha overwrites it (latest push wins, one slot). resetPrHead consumes (deletes) it when a head with that exact sha arrives — from the synchronize webhook or from resync's GitHub read alike. A push for the CURRENT head never touches this slot (it only takes back). Keyed by sha, so a stale slot can only ever describe the commit it names.

blockedAttempts.semantics: The fixAttempts value the last pr-blocked was published for. reduceCiEmission publishes pr-blocked only when fixAttempts >= maxFixAttempts AND fixAttempts !== blockedAttempts, then records fixAttempts here. A take-back whose pre-decrement fixAttempts equals blockedAttempts deletes it (the spec's 'a pr-blocked published for that count is forgotten').

stateFields.versioning: LegionState.version 24 -> 25: `version: 25` in the interface, z.literal(25), newLegionState, the `version !== 25` guard in loadState, and migrateV24State appended to the migrations list.

decisions.decision: Add `{ kind: "log"; message: string }` to the `Effect` union in reducers.ts (line ~22). events.ts `dispatch` (line ~622, the exhaustive `never` switch) executes it as `console.warn(`[legion] ${effect.message}`)`.
decisions.why: Reducers are pure and have no logger; the executor already centralizes effect application with a compile-time exhaustiveness check, so a new kind cannot be silently dropped. The alternative — a classification helper re-run in events.ts to decide whether to log — would duplicate reducer logic (PR lookup, verdict/headCounted checks) in the executor and could drift. A log effect is also directly assertable in reducers.test.ts (Acceptance 3). It cannot fail, so the durable lane's dispatch-before-save contract is unaffected. collapseClosedTreeWakes passes it through (it only filters `controller` effects).

decisions.decision: The three PrState fields are optional; migrateV24State is `if (!recordValue(state) || state.version !== 24) return state; return { ...state, version: 25 };` (the migrateV14State / migrateV21State precedent).
decisions.why: Absent IS the correct starting value for every existing record (no head with a take-back pending, no push pending, no pr-blocked recorded), so no per-record backfill exists to write. It also leaves the ~10 PrState literals in tests (api.test.ts x2, catchup.test.ts, ci-fixtures.ts, envelope-goldens.test.ts, events.test.ts, index.test.ts, legion-state.test.ts, reducers.test.ts addPr, resync.test.ts) untouched. Both required-nullable and optional fields already coexist in PrState (ciSettledAt vs headUpdatedAt/reviewDecision), so this is not a second convention.

decisions.decision: On take-back: `if (pr.blockedAttempts === pr.fixAttempts) delete pr.blockedAttempts; pr.fixAttempts -= 1; delete pr.headCounted;` — compare against the PRE-decrement count.
decisions.why: This is the spec Design text ('a pr-blocked published for that count is forgotten'): the count being taken back is the one whose publish becomes wrong. Forgetting the post-decrement count instead would make the head's next red settlement re-publish pr-blocked for a count already announced (violates Acceptance 4). See concerns[3] for the accepted interleaving.

decisions.decision: classifyPush reads changed_paths_truncated FIRST: absent => unknown 'changed_paths absent (listener predates LEGION-33)'; "true" => unknown 'changed_paths truncated at 100'; any other non-"false" value => unknown `changed_paths_truncated=<value> unrecognised`; then changed_paths absent/empty => unknown 'no commits listed'; otherwise split on "\n" and handoffOnly = every path startsWith(".legion/").
decisions.why: payloadJSON omits empty strings (normalize.go line ~995), so changed_paths is absent on the wire both for an old listener and for a new listener's empty-commits push; changed_paths_truncated is always non-empty from the new listener and is the reliable marker. The three spec reasons (field absent / list capped / no commits listed) remain distinguishable.

decisions.decision: Emit the log effect for an unclassifiable push only when the count is real: `pr.headSha === after ? pr.headCounted === true : pr.verdict === "red"`. Message: `fix attempt: ${pr.repo}#${pr.number} (${pr.key}) push ${after} to ${branch} could not be classified as handoff-only (${reason}); it counts against max_fix_attempts`.
decisions.why: Spec: 'logs which pull request it counted and why it could not tell'. Sync-first: headCounted says whether it was counted. Push-first: verdict red at push time is exactly the condition resetPrHead applies when the head arrives. A green PR with an old listener logs nothing because nothing was counted.

decisions.decision: resetPrHead's signature and its resync.ts:129 call stay unchanged; because the pending-slot consumption lives inside resetPrHead, a head first seen by resync whose sha matches pendingPush uses that classification.
decisions.why: The spec keeps resetPrHead 'unchanged' on the resync path and says resync counts as today because 'no push classification exists for it' — when one does exist (push webhook arrived, synchronize webhook lost), applying it is the same single rule, not a second one. Locked by a resync.test.ts case.

decisions.decision: No handling of force pushes, branch deletions (all-zero `after`), or `created` pushes: the normalized payload carries none of those flags. A rebase-only force push lists the rebased commits' files and counts (as today); a branch-deletion push lands in pendingPush until the PR's `closed` event deletes the record.
decisions.why: YAGNI; the spec's classification rule decides every case deterministically.

decisions.decision: Delete the `refs/heads/legion/` early return at reducers.ts:792. The push handler resolves `state.prByBranch[`${repo}@${ref.slice("refs/heads/".length)}`]`; no PR => []. Non-legion branch pushes (main, tags) fall out naturally: no mapping.
decisions.why: One lookup replaces a prefix guard plus a lookup; a push on a legion branch with no registered PR is 'ignored, as today' (spec Errors).

steps.title: Envoy listener forwards changed paths on push (spec Acceptance 6)
files: packages/envoy/scripts/fixtures/github/push.json (raw golden input: add file lists to its one commit)
behaviour: Add `const maxPushChangedPaths = 100` and `func githubPushChangedPaths(body map[string]any) (paths []string, truncated bool)`: iterate sliceValue(body["commits"]) in order; for each mapValue(commit) iterate the keys "added", "removed", "modified" in that order; each stringValue item that is non-empty and not yet in a seen set is appended (first-seen order) while len(paths) < 100; a 101st UNIQUE path sets truncated=true (keep scanning with the seen set so duplicates never count as new). Only commits[] is read — never head_commit (it is one of the commits; GitHub caps commits at 2048).

In githubPayload's `case "push":` add `"changed_paths": strings.Join(paths, "\n")` and `"changed_paths_truncated": strconv.FormatBool(truncated)`. Nothing else in the push payload or summary changes. payloadJSON will drop changed_paths when empty; changed_paths_truncated is always present ("true"/"false").

steps.title: Reducers: classify pushes, count only real fixes, publish pr-blocked once per count (spec Acceptance 1-4, 7, 8)
behaviour: Effect union (reducers.ts ~22): add `| { kind: "log"; message: string }`. events.ts dispatch (~622): `else if (effect.kind === "log") console.warn(`[legion] ${effect.message}`);` before the `never` branch.

New `const HANDOFF_PATH_PREFIX = ".legion/"` and `function classifyPush(payload: JsonRecord): { handoffOnly: true } | { handoffOnly: false; unknown?: string }` implementing D4 exactly. `unknown` is set only when the push could not be classified; a mixed push (some path outside .legion/) is `{ handoffOnly: false }` with no `unknown` and never logs.

New `function push(state, payload, envelope): Effect[] | undefined` (sibling of prComment/review/pullRequest, wired into the `??` chain in reduceGithubEvent; the refs/heads/legion/ early return at ~792 and its comment are deleted — D8): return undefined unless payload.kind === "push"; read repo (stringValue(payload.repo)), ref, after; return [] unless repo && ref startsWith "refs/heads/" && after; branch = ref.slice(11); prKey = state.prByBranch[`${repo}@${branch}`]; pr = prKey && state.prs[prKey]; return [] if no pr. Then: (i) if pr.headSha === after: if classification.handoffOnly && pr.headCounted => take-back per D3 (`if (pr.blockedAttempts === pr.fixAttempts) delete pr.blockedAttempts; pr.fixAttempts -= 1; delete pr.headCounted;`); the pending slot is NOT touched in this branch. (ii) else pr.pendingPush = { sha: after, handoffOnly: classification.handoffOnly } (overwrite). Finally, if classification.unknown and the D5 condition holds (evaluated BEFORE any mutation in branch (i) — i.e. headCounted as it was on entry), return [{ kind: "log", message }] else [].

resetPrHead(pr, headSha) becomes: `const pending = pr.pendingPush; const handoffOnly = pending?.sha === headSha && pending.handoffOnly; if (pending?.sha === headSha) delete pr.pendingPush; if (pr.verdict === "red" && !handoffOnly) { pr.fixAttempts += 1; pr.headCounted = true; } else { delete pr.headCounted; }` followed by the existing head/CI resets. Signature unchanged; pullRequest (~746) and resync.ts (~129) callers unchanged (D6). A pending slot for a DIFFERENT sha is left in place (it describes a newer push whose synchronize has not arrived).
registerPr: no change (the new fields start absent).

reduceCiEmission: replace the tail with `if (pr.fixAttempts < config.maxFixAttempts || pr.blockedAttempts === pr.fixAttempts) return []; pr.blockedAttempts = pr.fixAttempts; return routeActive(state, pr.key, { type: "pr-blocked", pr: number, attempts: pr.fixAttempts }, envelope);` — recorded whether or not routeActive found a tree (the publish is the reducer's decision; a closed tree still gets its controller wake once).
Update the `Effect` doc comment (a log effect cannot fail) and the CI-view / resetPrHead doc comments to name the handoff rule in one sentence each.
tests: reducers.test.ts helpers: `pushPayload(overrides)` => { kind: "push", repo, ref: `refs/heads/${childBranch}`, after: "new-sha", before: "old-sha", pusher: "legion-implementer[bot]", head_subject: "implement: record handoff", commit_count: "1", compare_url: "https://example.invalid/compare", changed_paths: ".legion/implement.json", changed_paths_truncated: "false", ...overrides } delivered on topic `notifications.github.acme.widgets.push.branch.${childBranch}`; `syncPayload(sha)` => { kind: "pr", action: "synchronize", repo, number: String(prNumber), head_ref: childBranch, head_sha: sha }; `settleRed(state, sha, at)` => settleCiVerdict(state, pr, { verdict: "red", failing: ["worker-image"], failingStatuses: [], settledAt: at }, config, envelope) collecting effects. All cases start from rootState()+attachChild()+addPr({ verdict: "red", failing: ["worker-image"], ciSettledAt: 1 }) unless stated.

A1 'six handoff-only pushes on a red PR count nothing and never publish pr-blocked': for i in 1..6 with sha `h${i}`: effects(push h_i) then effects(sync h_i) then settleRed(h_i) — collect every effect; assert fixAttempts === 0 after each round, headCounted and pendingPush undefined after each round, and no effect payload with type "pr-blocked" across the run. Also a variant that alternates order per round (sync first on even rounds) with the same assertions.

A2 'a push touching a path outside .legion/ counts one attempt' : changed_paths "packages/daemon/src/daemon/reducers.ts\n.legion/implement.json" (mixed) then sync => fixAttempts 1, headCounted true, no log effect; a second `it` with changed_paths "README.md" only => 1.

A3 'an unclassifiable push counts as today and logs why' — table over payload variants, sync-first order (sync new-sha then push): (a) neither changed_paths nor changed_paths_truncated present; (b) changed_paths_truncated "true" with changed_paths of 100 `.legion/x${n}.json` lines; (c) changed_paths_truncated "false" and no changed_paths. Each: fixAttempts === 1 after sync, and the push returns exactly [{ kind: "log", message: expect.stringContaining(<reason>) }] whose message also contains "acme/widgets#17" and "LEGSMOKE-2". Reasons: 'changed_paths absent', 'truncated', 'no commits listed'. Plus one push-first case for (a): push returns the log effect (verdict red), sync then yields fixAttempts 1. Plus a green-PR case for (a): addPr({ verdict: "green" }), sync-first => no log effect and fixAttempts 0.

A4 'pr-blocked publishes once per exhausted count': addPr({ fixAttempts: 3, headSha: "h" , verdict: null }); settleRed(h, 1) => exactly one pr-blocked effect ({ attempts: 3 }) and pr.blockedAttempts === 3; settleCiVerdict green (settledAt 2) => no pr-blocked; settleRed(h, 3) => none; green (4); settleRed(h, 5) => none — one pr-blocked total across the five settlements. Extend the existing 'notifies the architect when settled CI red exhausts the retry budget' assertion with blockedAttempts === 3.

A7a 'a handoff-only push before its synchronize leaves fixAttempts unchanged': addPr({ fixAttempts: 3, verdict: "red", ciSettledAt: 1, blockedAttempts: 3 }); push(new-sha handoff) => pendingPush { sha: "new-sha", handoffOnly: true }; sync(new-sha) => fixAttempts 3, pendingPush undefined, headCounted undefined, blockedAttempts 3.

A7b 'a handoff-only push after its synchronize takes the attempt back': same start; sync(new-sha) => fixAttempts 4, headCounted true; push(new-sha handoff) => fixAttempts 3, headCounted undefined, blockedAttempts still 3 (4 !== 3, nothing forgotten); settleRed(new-sha) => no pr-blocked (3 already published).

A7c 'a take-back forgets a pr-blocked published for the taken-back count so the next real fix republishes it': same start; sync(new-sha) => 4; settleRed(new-sha, 2) => pr-blocked { attempts: 4 }, blockedAttempts 4; push(new-sha handoff) => fixAttempts 3, blockedAttempts undefined; then push(fix-sha, changed_paths "packages/daemon/src/daemon/reducers.ts") + sync(fix-sha) => fixAttempts 4; settleRed(fix-sha, 3) => pr-blocked { attempts: 4 } published again.
A7d 'a duplicate handoff-only push delivery takes back at most once': after A7b's take-back, deliver the same push again => fixAttempts stays 3.

A8 'the push that deletes .legion/ is handoff-only': changed_paths ".legion/implement.json
.legion/plan.json
.legion/review.json
.legion/test.json" then sync => fixAttempts 0.
'a push on a legion branch with no registered PR is ignored': rootState() with no addPr; push => [] and state.prs/prByBranch unchanged.

'a later push for a newer head does not disturb a counted current head, and its classification waits for that head': sync(h1) counts to 1 (headCounted); push(h2, real) => pendingPush { h2, false }, fixAttempts 1; push(h1 handoff, late) => take-back to 0 while pendingPush { h2 } stays; sync(h2) (verdict null now) => 0, pendingPush consumed.

envelope-goldens.test.ts 'counts the Go-normalized push golden as a real fix attempt': import push.json from packages/contracts/fixtures/github-envelopes; state with a registered red PR whose prByBranch maps `example-org/example-repo@main` (the golden's ref) to it; reduceGithubEvent(state, push.topic, {payload: push.payload, …}) then a synchronize for the golden's `after` => fixAttempts 1 and no log effect (proves the TS classifier reads exactly what the listener emits).

steps.title: Docs (spec Acceptance 5)
behaviour: packages/daemon/src/daemon/AGENTS.md — new bullet under '## Operational invariants' (there is no fix-attempt paragraph today): a fix attempt is a new head that arrives (synchronize webhook or resync read) on a PR whose last settled verdict is red AND whose push webhook did not classify it handoff-only — every path in the push's `changed_paths` under `.legion/`, `changed_paths_truncated` "false", list non-empty. Name the fields (`PrState.headCounted`, `pendingPush`, `blockedAttempts`), the either-order rule (push first: remembered, latest push wins; synchronize first: taken back when the handoff-only push arrives, forgetting a `pr-blocked` published for that count), the unknown rule (no `changed_paths_truncated` = listener predates LEGION-33, `"true"` = capped at 100, no `changed_paths` = no commits listed: counted as before and logged `[legion] fix attempt: <repo>#<n> (<KEY>) push <sha> … could not be classified …` via the `log` effect), that resync counts as before unless a pending classification names the head, and that `pr-blocked` is published once per exhausted count (`blockedAttempts`), never again on later red verdicts for the same count. Also add `log` to the events.ts row's effect description.

packages/envoy/AGENTS.md '## Topic shapes' — new bullet after the GitHub repository topics bullet: `push.branch.<ref>` / `push.tag.<ref>` payload fields: `kind: "push"`, `repo`, `ref`, `after`, `before`, `pusher`, `head_subject`, `commit_count`, `compare_url`, `changed_paths` (unique paths across every pushed commit's added, removed, and modified lists, first-seen order, newline-separated, at most 100; omitted when no commit is listed) and `changed_paths_truncated` ("true" when more than 100 unique paths were seen, else "false"). Envoy forwards what GitHub sent; what counts as a handoff is the daemon's rule.

skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md `pr-blocked` row (~line 240): payload `{type:"pr-blocked", pr, attempts}`; `attempts` counts heads pushed onto a red verdict that changed something outside `.legion/` (handoff-only pushes never count; a push the daemon cannot classify does); published once per exhausted count, not on every later red verdict.
